html:
Operation Searchlight was the Pakistan Army's planned crackdown on the Bengali nationalist movement, launched in Dhaka on the night of 25 March 1971.

After Yahya Khan's talks with Sheikh Mujibur Rahman ended without a deal, the generals decided on force. Yahya flew out of Dhaka. Tanks and troops then moved on the University of Dhaka, the Rajarbagh police lines and the headquarters of the East Pakistan Rifles. Students, police, teachers and many civilians were killed. Mujib was arrested, but his declaration of independence was sent out around midnight, on 26 March, which Bangladesh marks as Independence Day.

The plan was to crush the movement in days and to arrest or kill its leaders, students and Hindus. It failed to do so. The army spread out across East Pakistan, and the killing became the Bangladesh genocide. Bengali soldiers and police mutinied, and the Mukti Bahini took shape. Millions of refugees fled into India.
sum: Operation Searchlight was the Pakistan Army's planned crackdown on the Bengali nationalist movement, launched in Dhaka on the night of 25 March 1971.
